newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: CSM, Cargill in lactic acid cooperation.
newsitem.headline: CSM, Cargill in lactic acid cooperation.

text.p: Dutch food group CSM NV said on Wednesday it had reached agreement with Cargill Inc. of the U.S. to jointly build a lactic acid factory in the U.S.
CSM's unit PURAC and Cargill's North American Corn Milling Division would each take a 50 percent stake in the joint venture, the Dutch group said in a statement.
The factory will be built near Cargill's plant in Blair, Nebraska, and is expected to start operations in the first half of 1998.

The joint venture, which first was announced last May, will have initial annual production capacity of 34,000 tonnes of lactic acid which is used to produce polyactic acid (PLA), a raw material for degradable plastics. If necessary, capacity can be doubled in a relatively short time, CSM said.
No financial details of the joint venture were given.
